text:
maria: quick question — we keep seeing KV cache bloat for long-running sessions. curious if folks have tried session-boundary keying instead of full-session stickiness

sam: seen that too. what's the exact bloat pattern? is it fragmentation across prefixes or huge single-session allocations?

maria: mostly fragmentation + slow growth. example: a 30k-token convo causes ~1.6GB resident KV increase across GPUs, not freed until session TTL evicts everything.

lee: that matches the profiling I ran last week — lots of small prefix entries that never get reused outside that session. eviction churn is high.

maria: idea: switch cache key from (tenant, session_id, prefix_fingerprint) -> (tenant, session_boundary_id, prefix_fingerprint) where session_boundary_id is sliced every N tokens (eg. every 1024 tokens) so prefixes spanning long contexts are grouped by boundary.

kevin: interesting. so new keying = floor(session_offset / boundary_size). that would let prefixes reused in nearby windows co-locate. reduces number of unique keys for long sessions.

aisha: downside: could increase false reuse if two unrelated prompts happen in same window. need to test quality/regression.

maria: agreed. propose experiment: A) implement boundary-keying + TTL per boundary (shorter than session TTL) B) additive stickiness heuristic: hot prefixes pinned across 2 adjacent boundaries if hit-rate > 0.6. Measure memory, hit-rate, and output token divergence against baseline.

sam: sounds good. I can wire a quick flag in runtime to switch keying for a tenant. will need to expose boundary_size and hot_threshold tunables.

lee: also add metrics: prefixes_created_per_boundary, prefixes_evicted_per_boundary, avg_prefix_size, reuse_ratio_by_boundary. right now reuse_ratio is global and hides boundary effects.

ops-bot: deploy queued by sam for branch kv/boundary-keying at 2026-03-18T15:40Z. CI: 4 checks passing, 1 flaky test skipped.

maria: first local perf snapshot (toy model, x1 GPU): baseline (session-key): memory 2.1GB, reuse_ratio 0.22, p50 latency 45ms. boundary-keying(1024): memory 1.3GB, reuse_ratio 0.46, p50 48ms.

kevin: small latency hit but big memory win — promising. what about quality? diffed logits on next-token across eval set?

maria: quick check: sampling divergence ~0.0025 KL on a 1k prompt set. seems acceptable but need broader eval.

lee: watch out for eviction storms: if many boundaries expire at same time, we might get bursty loads. add jitter to boundary TTLs or stagger expiry windows.

sam: implemented jittered TTL: base_ttl = boundary_ttl +/- rand(0, boundary_ttl/4). also added controlled prefetch for popular prefixes (top-k per tenant) to reduce cold-miss latency.

aisha: for cache key naming let's adopt: key = "kv_v2|{tenant}|b:{boundary}|p:{prefix_fp}". versioning helps rollback.

maria: good call. also instrumented a small profiler that logs prefix residency timeline like: 
```
[prof] prefix_fp=0x3a12 TTL_expire=1768903300 hits=8 size=24KB created=1768899800
```

lee: can we add a cheap fingerprint normalization so very similar prefixes don't split? maybe use truncated sha + context-length bucket. reduces entropy.

kevin: truncation helps but increases collision risk. use 64-bit xxhash + 2-bit length bucket, collision safe enough for reuse heuristics.

maria: next steps: run canary on small tenant cohort (dev and staging) for 48h, collect metrics, and run eval suite for quality. if memory < 1.5GB and reuse_ratio > 0.4 and KL < 0.01 -> promote.

sam: I'll roll the canary today. config flags: 
```
kv.keying=boundary
kv.boundary_size=1024
kv.boundary_ttl=3600
kv.hot_threshold=0.6
kv.prefetch_top_k=20
kv.jitter=true
```

aisha: add alert if eviction_rate spikes > 3x baseline or if p95 latency increases > 20%.

ops-bot: canary deployment started: kv/boundary-keying -> cluster gpu-pool-canary-1 at 2026-03-18T16:05Z.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary in #eng-runtime after 24h with numbers. anyone want to pair on the eviction graphing?

lee: I'll help, can do the Grafana dashboard tiles for per-boundary metrics.

kevin: and I'll add the hash/truncation change to the keying PR and run collision sim.

sam: ping me if any perf regressions show up, rolling back will be one flag flip.

maria: perfect. if this works we might generalize to tenant-adaptive boundary_size (long-session tenants get larger boundaries).

kevin: cool — also add a note in docs describing tradeoffs so solutions-engineering knows what to expect.

maria: sounds good. ending thread for now, will update with canary metrics. :thumbsup:
